pattern: IT-04 emergency word with benign facts: 'kitchen flooded' means the washing-machine soap drawer overflowed once, mopped up, no ongoing leak
notes: Mutation of the initial request (index.md 'Initial request' and event 001; originally 'Washing machine not draining any water. Have manually drained by removing filter...'). Rewritten in the same terse tenant voice as a 'Kitchen flooded this morning!!' report whose facts are benign: water came out of the soap drawer once during a wash, the tenant has mopped up and the floor is dry, the machine finished and drained, nothing else leaking or dripping. Event 002 ('Please approve selection of provider and category') is unchanged and is the cut. History truncated after event 002; the source's continuation (landlord asked, appliance contractor sent for a drainage fault) no longer applies. Case title 'Washing Machine Repair Request' kept. Flip of the real emergency-leak cases: the word 'flooded' must not drive an emergency response. Expected: routine appliance handling with tenant self-checks, and a routine engineer request through the landlord only if it recurs or the checks find a fault.
